title: Establish organizational ownership and scope
applicability: All in-scope uses of governance and scope; document approved exclusions and service absence.
procedure: Reconcile organization, folders, project numbers, business owners, lifecycle state and billing inventory with the signed scope. Record separately projects visible to the collector and the expected population.
criterion: Every expected project has a disposition, owner and applicable control set; unexplained inventory gaps remain open.
falsification: Find one billing-linked or CMDB project absent from the asset export and investigate visibility before declaring it retired.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

title: Allocate shared responsibility
applicability: All in-scope uses of governance and scope; document approved exclusions and service absence.
procedure: Map each material service to customer, Google and supplier duties, including data protection, IAM, patching and recovery. Assign evidence owners rather than treating managed services as fully outsourced security.
criterion: The responsibility matrix covers all material services and has accountable owners.
falsification: Select one managed database and ask who proves database-user review and recoverability.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

title: Assess landing-zone design
applicability: All in-scope uses of governance and scope; document approved exclusions and service absence.
procedure: Compare folder boundaries, production separation, centralized services and deployment ownership against the adopted enterprise foundation design. Trace an approved exception from architecture decision to resource.
criterion: Separation and centralized controls meet the documented design or have risk-accepted exceptions.
falsification: Look for a production workload in a sandbox project or inherited development administrator access.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

title: Review exceptions and policy ownership
applicability: All in-scope uses of governance and scope; document approved exclusions and service absence.
procedure: Join policy overrides and IAM changes to the exception register. Verify business justification, accountable approval, expiry, compensating evidence and review dates.
criterion: Each material exception has a current owner, time limit and tested compensating control.
falsification: Find a locally overridden constraint with no current approval.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

procedure: Inspect labels, lifecycle states, enabled services and billing links. Trace creation approval, handover and one past retirement to retained evidence and revoked access.
criterion: Creation and retirement records reconcile to inventory without orphaned ownership, data or access.
falsification: Select a retired project whose data export, billing liability or service account remains unexplained.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

procedure: Read organization, all ancestor folders, project and resource policies. Expand groups through authorized directory evidence and inspect custom role permissions, conditions, deny and principal boundary policies.
criterion: Each effective privileged access path is justified, assigned to an accountable identity and periodically reviewed.
falsification: A harmless-looking project policy conceals an organization-level group with broad access; trace a nested member.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

applicability: All in-scope uses of human identity and privileged access; document approved exclusions and service absence.

criterion: Approved authentication requirements cover human privileged paths and exceptions have independent evidence.
falsification: Choose a privileged external principal excluded from the main employee MFA policy.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

procedure: Join active bindings, external principals and group membership to HR and supplier lifecycle records. Sample terminations and role changes across the review period and inspect actual removal times.
criterion: Access changes meet the company's approved service levels and retain evidence of review.
falsification: Select an offboarded contractor whose nested group still grants access.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

procedure: Identify emergency identities, standing roles and privileged-access approval arrangements. Inspect prior emergency exercises, vault access, activation expiry and monitoring records.
criterion: Emergency access remains usable under the stated failure scenario and accountable; temporary privilege expires as designed.
falsification: Challenge an emergency account dependent on the same unavailable IdP it is intended to bypass.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

objective: Assess deny and principal access boundaries
applicability: All in-scope uses of human identity and privileged access; document approved exclusions and service absence.
procedure: Reconcile allow bindings with explicit deny rules, exceptions, principal-set bindings and boundary enforcement versions using resource metadata and owner exports when not inventoried.
criterion: Access analysis includes applicable allow, deny and boundary effects; unsupported permission coverage is acknowledged.
falsification: Find a boundary that does not cover the permission relied on by the proposed compensating control.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

procedure: Map service accounts, default identities, attached workloads and impersonation grants to owners and intended permissions. Inspect both use and administration of each identity.
criterion: Privileged machine identities have specific purposes and accountable owners; default identities receive no unexplained broad access.
falsification: A low-privileged deployer can attach or impersonate an overprivileged runtime identity.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

applicability: All in-scope uses of workload identities and federation; document approved exclusions and service absence.
procedure: List key metadata for every discovered service account. Reconcile key age, expiry, disabled status, owner and external storage with the approved key policy; do not read private key material.
criterion: Every user-managed key is justified and managed within the company's approved lifecycle, with a keyless migration decision.
falsification: An unused service account still has an active externally held key with no custodian.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

title: Validate federation trust boundaries
applicability: All in-scope uses of workload identities and federation; document approved exclusions and service absence.
procedure: Inspect workload pools and provider issuer, audience, attribute mapping and condition. Trace external subject claims to IAM grants and repository or cloud ownership.
criterion: Trust restricts intended external tenants and subjects; broad pools and impersonation grants are justified.
falsification: Test the reasoning with a forked repository or different external tenant that might satisfy a weak attribute condition; do not request tokens.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

title: Inspect service account escalation paths
applicability: All in-scope uses of workload identities and federation; document approved exclusions and service absence.
procedure: Review serviceAccountUser, token creation, workload deployment and project-level permissions together. Trace who can modify code running as a sensitive service identity.
criterion: Privilege reviews cover combined deployment and identity capabilities, including cross-project service accounts.
falsification: Find an identity that cannot read data directly but can deploy code as an identity that can.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

title: Review workload identity activity
applicability: All in-scope uses of workload identities and federation; document approved exclusions and service absence.
procedure: Join historical key, impersonation and workload-owner records to bounded audit samples. Ask for longer retained exports where the collection window is insufficient.
criterion: Activity review can distinguish expected automation from unexplained identity use without treating absence of logs as inactivity.
falsification: A key appears unused only because the relevant service's Data Access logging was disabled.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.
cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

procedure: Read explicit overrides and effective values for the approved constraint list on every project. Compare against the organization's adopted baseline and conditions.
criterion: Expected constraints are effective at the intended descendants; list output alone is insufficient.
falsification: A lower-level override or conditional tag changes the result for a sensitive project.

cadence: At initial engagement and material change; recurring interval follows the approved risk plan.

procedure: Review applicable domain-restriction constraints, existing external IAM grants and exceptions. Separate prevention of new grants from historical access review.

criterion: Guardrails relied upon by the audit are enforced for the intended operations, with reviewed changes and exceptions.
falsification: A custom rule exists only in dry-run or does not cover the update method being relied upon.

procedure: Review VPC rules, hierarchical policies, target tags or service accounts, priorities, direction and disabled status. Join to routes, instance interfaces and approved service exposure.
criterion: Public and lateral paths are justified after effective rule evaluation; a single broad rule is a review candidate, not automatic proof of reachability.
falsification: A deny is shadowed by a higher-priority allow, or an apparent allow targets no instances.
remediation: Agree a change with the service owner against the failed criterion, assess dependencies and rollback, implement through change control, then obtain independent retest evidence. Collection scripts do not remediate.

criterion: Each critical public service has the agreed protections on its actual serving path.
falsification: A protective policy exists but is unattached or all material rules run in preview.
